thread:
jun: heads-updid a more granular bring-up of nova-emb-v2 (fp16 -> int6). overall recall@10 drop small (0.938 -> 0.901) but short-tail recall@1 (query tokens <=5) collapsed more than expected: 0.79 -> 0.55. reproducible across two seeds.

maya: thanks. did you use same calibration set as before? any difference in tokenizers for short queries?

jun: calibration 5k stratified by length, tokenizer unchanged. quant config: per_channel_symmetric int6, clip by percentile 99.9, no LN quant. eval pipeline: no query-time L2 norm.

anand: can you post the quick stats + idflip histogram? if top-1 flips a lot it's probably margin collapse, not info loss.

jun: pasted core table and a tiny idflip summary.

```text
global: recall@1 0.748 -> 0.612
recall@5 0.872 -> 0.835
recall@10 0.938 -> 0.901
short(<=5) r@1 0.79 -> 0.55
idflip@1 (pct queries with different top1): 6.8% overall, 18.4% short
mean cosine drop (top1): 0.032 overall, 0.078 short
```

soph: that's a pretty high idflip for short queries. curious if batch size during calibration changed the activation distribution. also check k=10 neighbourhood overlap vs baseline.

jun: ran neighbourhood overlap (Jaccard) for top10: overall 0.86, short 0.64. also tried L2-normalize at search time and short r@1 moved to 0.60.

maya: ok that points at geometry shift. try whitening + tiny per-dim scale (median scaling) and L2 norm; that trick reclaimed to ~0.66 in earlier int8 work. also put the final LN params in fp8 (instead of fp16) to see if that helps.

anand: add per-tensor int6 sweep as baselineif per-tensor reduces variance maybe it's a safer trade for short-tail correctness. include 10k and 50k calibration sizes.

ops-bot: perf metrics: int6 per-channel gives 1.9x throughput vs fp16 at batch=128 on staging, memory down -32%. per-tensor int6 slightly slower (1.7x) but similar mem.

jun: quick experiments I kicked off:
- run_8812: per-tensor int6 + 5k calib (queued)
- run_8813: per-channel int6 + 20k calib + whitening+rescale (running)
- run_8814: per-channel int6 + final-LN-fp8 (running)

ci-bot: run artifacts for 8813 uploaded -> https://internal.ci/firebrand/runs/20260210-091000 (artifacts: recall_breakdown.csv, idflip_hist.png, umap_shorttail.html)

maya: grabbing the umap now. if short queries concentrate into tight micro-clusters that shift a bit with quantization that's consistent with higher idflip rates. I'll generate a small interactive html with hover-to-see-query.

soph: also add cross-lingual short query check (en/es/pt) and an STS-like cosine correlation test (pearson r) between fp16 vs int6 embeddings to see linear relationship.

jun: did a quick pearson on a 2k sample: r=0.93 overall, but for short queries r=0.76.

anand: that gap is telling. for acceptance criteria we should set: overall recall@10 drop <= 0.03 AND short r@1 delta <= 0.08 AND idflip@1 short <= 12%. otherwise fallback to fp16 for short-query routing.

maya: good acceptance criteria. we can also consider hybrid serving: use int6 for queries >5 tokens, fp16 for short. Ops implications?

ops-bot: hybrid possible with routing rule (query_length <=5 -> fp16). perf hit depends on percent short traffic; estimate: short queries are ~9% of production qps so capacity impact ~+6% (still net win). created ticket INF-8357 for hybrid rollout plan.

ci-bot: logs attached for all runs -> https://internal.ci/firebrand/runs/ (search run_8812..8814)

jun: next steps: finish per-tensor run, analyze 20k calib whitening run, generate idflip-per-lang. I'll post summary by EOD and recommend either accept int6 with whitening + L2-normalize, or enable hybrid routing.

maya: I'll publish UMAP html and silhouette-by-length plots.

soph: I'll run the STS-B style correlation per-lang and push numbers to the run artifacts.

jun: thanks team. reconvene tomorrow after final numbers. :mag_right:
